title: Chicken Quesadilla
subtitle: Spiced chicken and melted cheese in a toasted flour tortilla
excerpt: Shredded spiced chicken and generous cheddar toasted between two flour tortillas until golden and crisp. A fast, satisfying meal that takes the cheese quesadilla one step further.
sourceNotes: Chicken quesadillas: a Tex-Mex home-cooking standard. The double-tortilla sandwich format rather than the folded single-tortilla is the American diner convention. Based on classic Tex-Mex home-cooking sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and shred the chicken a day ahead; reheat in a dry pan before assembling.

content.text: Chicken quesadillas use two flour tortillas sandwiched together with shredded spiced chicken and cheese, toasted flat in a pan. The filling goes between two tortillas rather than inside one folded one, which makes the quesadilla easier to cut and hold. The chicken cooks and shreds in 15 minutes before the pan comes out again for toasting.
Grate the cheese finely; it melts more evenly than coarser grating and reaches the edges of the tortilla without gaps.

Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, and salt. Toss the chicken thighs through the mixture. Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the thighs for 6-7 minutes each side. Rest 5 minutes. Shred finely with two forks.
Wipe the pan clean. Heat over medium heat (no oil). Lay one flour tortilla flat in the pan.
Scatter half the cheese over the entire surface. Spread half the shredded chicken evenly on top. Lay a second tortilla on top and press down gently.

Cook for 2 minutes without touching until the bottom is golden. Flip carefully and cook 1.5-2 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted. Slide onto a board, rest 1 minute, then cut into wedges.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas, chicken, and cheese. Serve with soured cream, spring onion, and jalapeño if using.

items.cause: Not enough cheese to bind, or flipped too soon
items.fix: The cheese acts as glue; wait until the bottom is properly golden before flipping. A large spatula underneath the whole quesadilla and a gentle press with the hand on top makes the flip more controlled.

items.cause: Thighs overcooked, or shredded while very hot
items.fix: Pull the thighs at just-cooked and rest for 5 minutes before shredding. If the chicken looks dry, a squeeze of lime juice after shredding adds moisture.

items.cause: Too much chicken filling, or heat too high and outside burned before heat reached centre
items.fix: Use a moderate amount of chicken per quesadilla. Medium heat gives the filling time to warm through before the outside burns.

items.symptom: Tortilla goes soft and leathery rather than crisp
items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or too much filling creating steam
items.fix: Heat the dry pan properly before the tortilla goes in. A little steam from the filling is normal; too much means the filling is too wet.

content.text: Chicken quesadillas appear on nearly every Tex-Mex restaurant menu in the US and have become a weeknight staple wherever flour tortillas are sold. The double-tortilla sandwich format comes from the US. In Mexico, a quesadilla is usually a single folded corn tortilla. Both work well. The double version is easier to handle when the filling is generous.
